target_customer: Developers and engineering teams running background tasks, AI agents and workflows (customers listed include Cursor, Linear, Motion, SpaceX)
problem: Teams need reliable, observable task queues and workflow orchestration without running Celery, Temporal or custom infrastructure.
business_model: Open source core (MIT) with usage-based cloud and enterprise support
product_category: Task queue and workflow orchestration platform for developers

founders.name: Alexander Belanger
education: University of Pennsylvania, BA Physics and Computer Science
founders.background_notes: Worked on task queues and distributed systems at Oneleet (YC page).

founders.name: Gabe Ruttner
education: Cornell, Master's in CS and AI

technical_complexity.rationale: A reliable distributed queue and DAG engine on Postgres with gRPC workers and low latency; the founders had to solve scaling and durability.

defensibility.rationale: Once embedded in an application's task layer it is hard to remove, but MIT licensing lets hyperscalers or rivals offer it, a risk the founders acknowledged.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Temporal and others kept competing and Hatchet kept growing.

market_need_then: Developers complained about Celery and heavy workflow engines; the Show HN drew 578 points in early 2024, showing demand for a simple Postgres queue.

branding.domain_note: hatchet.run, a .run TLD because the plain word is crowded; purchase story not found

identity.logo: Brand assets listed on Brandfetch; design not described in sources
identity.visual_style: Developer tool minimal; site uses Bong Cat illustrations

branding.community_and_virality: Open source repo and Hacker News Show HN and Launch HN posts; blog posts like two years of open source.

brand_strength.rationale: Real word with a developer feel, but generic for search and no mascot or independent press on the brand.

pivots.to: Orchestration platform for AI agents, background tasks and workflows
pivots.why: Positioning grew from task queue to agent and workflow orchestration as AI workloads rose (company site)

outcome_analysis: Hatchet, an open source Postgres task queue launched on Hacker News in early 2024, grew into an agent and workflow orchestration platform. The company announces a 5.7M seed with v2 and lists logos such as Cursor, Linear and SpaceX, plus 170M tasks run daily. Open source distribution and AI workload growth drove adoption. No shutdown or acquisition found.
notes: The 5.7M seed is stated on hatchet.run alongside Hatchet v2; its date and investors were not found, and one cross-check search returned no press for it, so it rests on the company's own site. Aggregators list an earlier pre-seed or convertible note of about 500K (Caplight 2024-02-27 with Hawk Hill Ventures, Ritual Capital and YC; VCBacked with Liquid 2 Ventures; CB Insights convertible note), unverified and not recorded as a round. Customer logos are the company's claims. Name origin not found.
